title: Keating v. Warrior Presbytery
disposition_detail: The SJC sustained the appeal on procedural grounds, reversed and voided the divestiture, and remanded for appropriate action. It sustained the allegation that Presbytery hurried to decision before hearing all testimony but rejected the reasonable-indulgence allegation. Keating remained a minister in good standing; Presbytery could reconsider divestiture under BCO 34-10.
first_summary: Keating challenged Warrior Presbytery’s decision to divest him of ordination without censure while he was absent. The SJC sustained his appeal, voided the divestiture, and remanded because Presbytery proceeded without hearing his defense as required by BCO 34-10. Keating remained a minister in good standing, although Presbytery could reconsider divestiture after giving him an adequate opportunity to respond.
summary: Keating challenged Warrior Presbytery’s decision to divest him of ordination without censure while he was absent. The SJC sustained his appeal, reversed and voided the divestiture, and remanded because BCO 34-10’s required opportunity to be heard in his defense was not provided; this also amounted to hurrying before all testimony was taken. It rejected the reasonable-indulgence claim because Presbytery did not know of his postponement request. Keating remained a minister in good standing, but Presbytery could reconsider divestiture after reasonably soliciting a defense.
